property_summary: For any caller, c.owner() must return the contract's stored (nonzero) deployer owner; the mutant returns address(0) for every caller, breaking the rule.
After transferring ownership to any nonzero fuzzed address, c.owner() must return exactly that address; the mutant's owner() always returns the zero address, breaking this for every nonzero newOwner.

For any nonzero fuzzed address, the current owner can transfer ownership to it and afterwards c.owner() must equal that address; the mutant's owner() always returns address(0), so transferOwnership reverts for every caller and the check fails.

For any caller, renounceOwnership() succeeds exactly when the caller is the deployer (the stored owner), and fails otherwise; the mutant's owner() returning the zero address makes _checkOwner fail for every caller, so even the deployer's renounce reverts.

From the deployer (the stored owner), calling setCaller with any nonzero address must succeed, because _checkOwner passes for the real owner; the mutant's owner() returns address(0), so every setCaller call reverts and the rule fails for all admissible inputs.

For any caller, c.owner() must return the fixed stored owner (the deployer set at construction), independent of the caller; the mutant returns msg.sender, so a call from any address other than the deployer yields the caller instead of the owner.

For every non-owner address, owner-gated functions like setCaller must revert (only the stored owner may pass the onlyOwner check); the mutant makes owner() return msg.sender, so the check always passes and a non-owner's setCaller succeeds without reverting.

After the deployer calls transferOwnership(newOwner), c.owner() must return the stored new owner no matter who calls it; the mutant returns msg.sender, so a third party's call returns the caller instead.

In the reference, owner() always returns the fixed stored owner (the deployer, address(this)) regardless of caller, so only that owner can renounceOwnership and owner() stays address(this); the mutant returns msg.sender, letting any other actor successfully renounce (or see themselves as owner), so owner() deviates from the stored owner.

For any two distinct callers, c.owner() returns the same fixed stored owner (owner-gated identity is caller-independent); the mutant returns msg.sender, so two different callers observe different owners.

Only the current owner may transfer ownership: a transferOwnership call from a non-owner must revert and leave owner() unchanged; the mutant lets any caller change the owner, breaking this for some caller.
